prompt: Complete TopWords.longestN so it returns the n longest words, ordered by length descending with alphabetical order breaking ties, using a sorted stream and limit.
explanation: sorted(comparator) orders the stream without touching the source list, and limit(n) then keeps only the first n elements -- together they express 'top n by some order'. The comparator chains three ideas: comparingInt(String::length) sorts by length, reversed() flips that to descending, and thenComparing(naturalOrder()) resolves equal lengths alphabetically. Note that reversed() is applied before the tie-breaker is attached, so only the length ordering is flipped, not the alphabetical one.
hints: Chain .thenComparing(java.util.Comparator.naturalOrder()) AFTER reversed() so ties are alphabetical ascending; limit(n) handles both n = 0 and n larger than the list.
